IR.rationale: A 5Y-FedFunds spread that widens while bill rates are not rising points to a higher term premium without policy tightening. Forward-spread regressions find that this state is followed by higher bond excess returns.

B.rationale: High-yield returns summarise the risk-appetite and credit-premium state, which co-moves with the risk premia priced in the Treasury curve and in IG spreads.

V.rationale: High oil uncertainty signals growth risk and safe-haven demand. Calm gold volatility means inflation and monetary-hedging fears are absent, which favours duration.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equity strength reflects global dollar liquidity and reserve-manager demand for Treasuries, which affects term premia.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to government bond returns.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength tightens global conditions and is disinflationary through import prices, which tends to lower US yields.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices lower inflation expectations and breakevens, which supports nominal bond prices.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions together with stable or falling inflation expectations describe a deflationary flight-to-quality state that favours Treasuries.

ENDG.rationale: Bond indices show time-series momentum at weekly to quarterly horizons, though some short-run reversal is possible.

IR.rationale: A bear steepening of both the policy-anchored and long segments of the curve signals repricing of the rate path and term premium. Such repricing tends to cluster into turbulent periods.

B.rationale: Weak high-yield returns mark deteriorating risk appetite, which precedes large flight-to-quality and reversal moves in rates.

V.rationale: Gold implied volatility captures uncertainty about real rates and inflation hedging. It is the volatility gauge most closely tied to future rate volatility.

AP.rationale: Equity declines raise uncertainty and trigger portfolio rebalancing into and out of duration, which raises bond volatility (leverage and flight-to-quality effects).

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no direct mechanism linking them to bond variance.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation tightens global funding conditions and can force reserve managers to sell Treasuries, adding to rate volatility.

COM.rationale: Commodity returns add little information on bond variance beyond the volatility and macro groups.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean reduced dealer balance-sheet capacity and more uncertainty, which predicts higher realised rate volatility.

ENDG.rationale: Variance clusters but mean-reverts, so a high recent level carries information about excess future variance.

IR.rationale: A bear steepening of 10Y-2Y signals a rising term premium and selling of duration, which tends to persist and produce large losses on longer bonds.

B.rationale: Weak EM sovereign bonds point to global dollar tightening and reserve selling, which can spill over into US rate selloffs.

V.rationale: High gold volatility reflects uncertainty about inflation and real rates, which raises the chance of a sharp bond selloff.

AP.rationale: Value outperformance marks a reflation trade with rising growth and inflation expectations, a state associated with rising yields.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to bond tail losses.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar is associated with reflation and reduced foreign demand for Treasuries, which raises the risk of large bond losses.

COM.rationale: Oil price jumps push up inflation expectations and breakevens, which raises nominal yields.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens signal inflation repricing and possible policy tightening, the main driver of large bond losses.

ENDG.rationale: Recent poor returns tend to continue through bond-market momentum and investor outflows, raising the probability of tail losses.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates signal expected easing or safe-haven demand at the front end, which precedes strong duration rallies.

B.rationale: Movements in the high-grade spread capture flight-to-quality shifts between corporate and Treasury debt, which are relevant to large rallies.

V.rationale: Broad risk-off uncertainty across equity and oil markets triggers flight-to-quality demand for Treasuries.

AP.rationale: Equity weakness and the negative stock-bond correlation make large bond gains more likely after equity selloffs.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no direct mechanism linking them to large bond gains.

FX.rationale: A falling Australian dollar is a risk-off and global-growth-scare signal, which is associated with safe-haven bond rallies.

COM.rationale: Oil weakness lowers inflation expectations and signals growth fears, both of which favour large Treasury gains.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise the odds of policy easing and flight to quality, which drive sharp bond rallies.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent returns tend to persist through bond time-series momentum, raising the chance of a further large gain.
